content: Internal Revenue Service, Compliance Division. This is Agent Peterson. How can I assist you today?
Hi, um, I got a voicemail that said something about my taxes and an urgent situation. I'm not sure what this is about.
Thank you for calling back promptly. According to our records, there is a serious issue from your previous tax filings. We recently conducted an audit and found discrepancies in your returns.
An audit? I just graduated last year, so I don't even know if I did anything wrong. I really don't have much income.

Unfortunately, the system shows you owe a significant balance due to underreported income and failure to file properly. The matter has escalated, and you are now at risk of enforcement action if unresolved.
What? I thought I paid my taxes already. Is there a way I can check this?

I understand this is overwhelming, but we're past the point of verification. The IRS has already issued a final notice. If this isn't immediately settled, your wages could be garnished, and your bank accounts frozen. There may even be a warrant for your arrest.
No, no, please! I can't have my accounts frozen. I have student loans to pay and barely enough to get by.
I sympathize, but my hands are tied. The outstanding balance, including penalties and late fees, is $5,400. To avoid further escalation, you must settle this today.
I don't have that kind of money! Is there anything I can do? Can I make a payment plan?

Due to the severity, payment plans are no longer available through the IRS portal. However, our department can process an emergency one-time payment through verified channels. This must be handled before close of business today, or enforcement will proceed.
What do you mean by verified channels? I don't understand.

For cases flagged at this stage, you must either complete a direct wire transfer, purchase government-approved prepaid gift cards, or initiate a crypto transfer. These are the only accepted methods for urgent resolution.
Gift cards? That doesn't sound normal for taxes.

Under certain circumstances, the IRS uses third-party processing for rapid collections. Do not discuss this with anyone; outside interference could lead to immediate escalation, including asset seizure.
I... I don't want my assets seized. I barely have anything. How do I do this?

Here's what you need to do: Go to the nearest grocery store or pharmacy and purchase $5,400 in Apple or Target gift cards. Stay on the line with me as you do this, so I can guide you through the process.
But... that's a lot of money. I don't even know if my card will let me buy that much.
If you cannot purchase the full amount, buy as much as your card allows. We can process the balance through a Zelle or PayPal transfer if needed. What is your available credit limit?
I think I have about $2,000 on my card. The rest I don't know.
Understood. Purchase $2,000 in gift cards now and let me know the denominations. For the remainder, I will send you wire instructions or a secure crypto wallet address.
This still feels strange. Why can't I just go online and pay like normal?
Because your case is under legal review. Any deviation from these instructions will be flagged as non-compliance and immediately reported. Do you wish to resolve this or risk arrest?
No, no, I'll try to get the gift cards. Do I just read you the numbers when I get them?
Correct. Once you have the cards, read each code to me. Do not hang up or speak to any store employees about this, doing so may delay the resolution and escalate your case.
Okay, I'll go now. Please don't let them arrest me.
Stay calm and follow my instructions exactly. As long as you comply, I can place a temporary hold on enforcement. Do not disconnect until payment is processed.
